newsitem.title: CHINA: China buys 60,000 T soymeal, interest wanes.
newsitem.headline: China buys 60,000 T soymeal, interest wanes.

text.p: China bought at least 60,000 tonnes of soybean meal on Wednesday after heavy purchases of soybeans and meal on Tuesday, Asian traders said.

China had bought at least 200,000 tonnes each of soybeans and soymeal on Tuesday as prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) dipped on weather news. Buying interest waned on Wednesday as the orders sent prices back up.
July soymeal on the CBOT settled $1.90 higher on Tuesday's news at $266.70 a tonne. Other months were down $2.30 to $4.00 a tonne.
One trader in Singapore said he sold close to 60,000 tonnes of soybean meal in three lots of 20,000, 20,000 and 18,000 tonnes on Wednesday at $292-294 per tonne.

The buyers were Chinese traders who had already received deposits from their customers and had the backing of major state-run corporations, he said, adding the cargoes were for late July/early August delivery. Origin was optional but likely to be Brazil.

He and other traders in Singapore, Hong Kong and China said that with the rise in nearby prices, Chinese buyers would stay away from the soy market until they saw prices for the new U.S. crop start to bottom out.
"The suppliers are reluctant to sell now because they are afraid of defaults," a Hong Kong trader said.
"There is still room for further falls," he said. "If it comes off another $10, the buyers will default."
Traders generally agreed that China's soymeal purchases since last week had reached 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes.
Soybeans would be off China's shopping list until prices fell to the low $280s, traders said.
With nearby prices still around $320 a tonne, there was little margin for Chinese buyers, one of the Hong Kong sources said.
New crop U.S. soybeans were around $287 a tonne, he said. "But again suppliers are cautious because we will see some falls in the second half of July when the situation is more clear".
Planting of soybean and corn crops is almost finished, with harvesting timed for September/October.
